workflow.title: Four roles, one traceable research pipeline
workflow.lede: Complex questions are no longer written in one pass by one model. Each role does one job and hands it on; when the reviewer finds a problem, the draft goes back for one revision.
workflow.planDesc: Understands the question and splits it into searchable sub-questions and an outline.
workflow.researchDesc: Searches the knowledge bases you selected and picks the relevant passages.
workflow.writeDesc: Writes from the evidence and cites a source for every conclusion.
workflow.reviewDesc: Checks each citation and claim and returns the draft for one revision if needed.
workflow.note: With a knowledge base connected and strict source mode on, comparison, review and summary questions switch to the four-role workflow automatically; open the answer's execution details to follow each role.

evidence.title: Every conclusion leads back to the source
evidence.lede: Each marker in an answer points to a specific passage in your knowledge base. Open it to see the text, page and position.
evidence.hybrid: Keyword and vector search run together, then a local reranker picks the most relevant passages.
evidence.locate: Citations resolve to the page and passage, with the source text highlighted.
evidence.honest: In strict source mode the assistant tells you when your sources do not support an answer instead of filling the gap.
evidence.demoQuestion: Why are gold nanorods better than nanospheres for refractive-index sensing?
evidence.demoAnswer: The longitudinal resonance of gold nanorods sits at longer wavelengths and responds more strongly to refractive-index changes
evidence.demoAnswerTail: ; the aspect ratio also tunes the resonance to the detection band.
evidence.demoSourceMark: the longitudinal plasmon resonance of gold nanorods lies at longer wavelengths and shows a higher sensitivity to the refractive index of the surrounding medium
evidence.link: Point at a marker to see the passage it refers to.

lspr.title: Put that answer on a spectrum
lspr.lede: The answer above says gold nanorods respond more strongly to the refractive index. Drag the slider to change the surrounding medium and compare how each particle's resonance peak moves.
lspr.index: Refractive index of the medium n
lspr.note: Illustrative model: Lorentzian line shapes whose peaks shift linearly with the index. Parameters are typical literature magnitudes for demonstration only, not measured data.
lspr.plotLabel: Illustrative extinction spectrum of a {particle} at refractive index {n}, resonance at {peak} nm

spec.title: Built for long-running research
spec.lede: Everything listed here is available in the current release.
spec.collabValue: Plan → research → write → review in a fixed order; one revision when review fails
spec.retrievalValue: Hybrid keyword and vector recall with a local reranker
spec.citationValue: Resolve to the document page and passage, with the source text highlighted
spec.embeddingValue: Local Chinese embedding model, runs offline
spec.tasksValue: Durable runs: they continue after you leave, can be stopped or given new instructions, and resume from checkpoints after a restart
spec.clarifyValue: Asks you first when information is missing, then continues
spec.memoryValue: Scoped to the project; traceable, correctable and deletable
spec.extendValue: Bring your own MCP servers and Skills; every call needs your approval
spec.faqValue: Standard answers linked to alternative phrasings, with inline editing, re-indexing and de-duplication
spec.modelsValue: Generation, embedding and rerank models at a glance; switch the generation model in chat
spec.isolationValue: Knowledge bases per account; conversations, tasks and memory per project
